aliases.name: Senapan Serbu 2
aliases.note: Indonesian for "Assault Rifle 2", the name SS2 abbreviates

massEmpty.sourceNote: Military Factory's SS2 spec listing gives 7.50 lb (3.40 kg) empty for the base SS2-V1; recorded as estimated rather than verified because the same listing's barrel-length figure is internally inconsistent with Wikipedia's own sourcing, which lowers confidence in the page generally. No Pindad-published figure for the base V1 was found — the manufacturer's own cited figures cover only the V2, V4, V5, SS3 and SPM-1 variants

length.sourceNote: Wikipedia infobox, uncited on Wikipedia itself, stock extended; corroborated by Military Factory's independently listed 990 mm overall length

lengthFolded.sourceNote: Wikipedia infobox, uncited on Wikipedia itself, stock folded

barrelLength.sourceNote: Wikipedia infobox 'part_length' for the SS2-V1, uncited on Wikipedia itself

cyclicRate.sourceNote: Wikipedia's infobox states 720-760 rpm (uncited on Wikipedia itself); Military Factory's independent spec listing states a single figure of 700 rpm, just outside that range

capacity.sourceNote: Wikipedia infobox describes 'various STANAG magazines'; Military Factory's spec listing gives a 20- or 30-round detachable box magazine, and 30 rounds is recorded here as the standard STANAG capacity

variants.name: SS2-V2
variants.summary: A carbine version of the SS2-V1 with a shorter barrel.

massEmpty.sourceNote: Wikipedia infobox, cited on Wikipedia to an Indonesian-language spec article (lancercell.com) whose ballistic-data table is presented as images rather than text and could not be independently re-read

length.sourceNote: Wikipedia infobox, uncited on Wikipedia itself, stock extended

lengthFolded.sourceNote: Wikipedia infobox, uncited on Wikipedia itself, stock folded

barrelLength.sourceNote: Wikipedia infobox 'part_length' for the SS2-V2, uncited on Wikipedia itself

variants.name: SS2-V4
variants.summary: The carrying handle is replaced with a Picatinny rail for scope mounting and the barrel lengthened and accurised, marketed as a designated-marksman configuration; 150 units were purchased by the Indonesian Army in 2007.

massEmpty.sourceNote: Wikipedia infobox, cited on Wikipedia to an Indonesian-language spec article (lancercell.com) whose ballistic-data table is presented as images rather than text and could not be independently re-read

length.sourceNote: Wikipedia infobox, uncited on Wikipedia itself, stock extended

lengthFolded.sourceNote: Wikipedia infobox, uncited on Wikipedia itself, stock folded

barrelLength.sourceNote: Wikipedia infobox 'part_length' for the SS2-V4, uncited on Wikipedia itself

variants.name: SS2-V5
variants.summary: A lighter, third-generation carbine with a folding-telescoping stock and Picatinny handguard rails, built for vehicle crews and airborne troops; ordered in large numbers by the Indonesian police.

massEmpty.sourceNote: Shephard Media's own reporting from Indo Defence 2016 states the SS2-V5 weighs 3.35 kg without magazine, matching the figure independently given in Wikipedia's infobox

barrelLength.sourceNote: Wikipedia infobox 'part_length' for the SS2-V5, uncited on Wikipedia itself

length.sourceNote: Wikipedia's infobox states 770 mm extended / 520 mm folded (uncited on Wikipedia itself); Shephard Media's own reporting instead states the rifle is 725 mm long, without specifying a stock position — the two published figures disagree and neither is preferred here

images.alt: A Pindad SS2-V1 assault rifle in right side profile: a black rifle with a carrying handle over the receiver, ribbed handguard, side-folding stock extended, and a curved STANAG magazine
images.caption: A Pindad SS2-V1, the base assault rifle configuration, photographed at Indo Defence 2008.

images.alt: An Indonesian soldier seen from behind, carrying a Pindad SS2 rifle slung across his back with its stock folded to the side
images.caption: An SS2 carried with its side-folding stock folded, showing the compact travelling configuration the folding stock is meant to provide.

images.alt: A kneeling U.S. Army soldier shows an Indonesian TNI soldier a Pindad SS2 rifle fitted with an optical sight during a joint range training exercise
images.caption: A U.S. Army soldier and a Tentara Nasional Indonesia (TNI) soldier with a rail-equipped SS2 during a Pindad SS2 assault rifle range as part of Super Garuda Shield 2022 at Baturaja Training Area, Indonesia.
